{"reconstruction": "Context: 'Litt. C.' continues the previous page. That page reduced four observations of a minor planet. It computed the Sun's longitudes l, l', l'', l'''; the geocentric longitudes α, α', α'', α'''; the latitudes b', b'' for the 2nd and 3rd observations only; and the logs of the solar distances R…R''' (0.0038571, 0.0065812, 0.0071415, 9.9998448). It ended with first-hypothesis values log P' = 0.0027955, log P'' = 9.9886858, log Q' = 9.2322405, log Q'' = 9.2463502, plus the constants a', a'', b' = −8.5509454 and b'' = −5.3744895.

This is Gauss's problem of determining an orbit from four observations of which only the middle two are complete (later Theoria Motus II, Sect. 4, arts. 164ff). The unknowns are the curtate distances x' and x'' at observations 2 and 3. Every quantity is in 7-place logarithms; a trailing 'n' marks a negative number.

(1) Coefficients of the two linear relations (two parallel columns, one per relation).
- First block, first column: log R' + log sec b' + log sin(l'−α) + log cosec(α''−α) = 0.0038571 + 0.0081674 + 9.8393488 + 1.0462222 = 0.8975955n, i.e. −7.8994255. The second column gives 0.7131598n, i.e. −5.1660643.
- Below these stand −0.6515199 and −0.2084252. Their derivation is not visible on the page.
- Second block, first column: log(R''/cos b'') + log sin(l''−α) + log cosec(α''−α) = 0.0117114 + 9.9877540 + 1.5669609 = 1.5664263, i.e. 36.849051. The second column gives 0.3776683, i.e. 2.3859884. Note that 0.0117114 = 0.0065812 + 0.0051302, i.e. R'' with sec b''; the second column's 0.0120245 = 0.0038571 + 0.0081674, i.e. R' with sec b'.
- 'Pars const.' Gauss first formed 36.849051 + 0.6515199 = 37.500571 and 2.3859884 + 0.2084252 = 2.5944136. He crossed both out: the small terms belong to the opposite columns. Re-done in the boxed computation: 36.849051 + 0.208425 = 37.057476 and 2.3859884 + 0.6515199 = 3.0375083.
- Coefficient of the P-term, first column: log R + log cos b'' + log sin(l−α) + log cosec(α''−α) = 9.9998448 + 0.0051302 + 9.2654636 + 1.5669609 = 0.8373995. Second column: 0.0071415 + 0.0081674 + 9.9922430 + 0.6107028 = 0.6182547. Adding log P' (resp. log P'') gives 6.9214175 (resp. 4.0452046).
- Constants: c' = 37.057476 + 6.921417 = 43.978893 and c'' = 3.0375083 + 4.0452046 = 7.0827129.
- Slope coefficients: log d' = log sin(α''−α) + log cosec(α'−α) + log(cos b'/cos b'') + log(1+P') = 0.5177015 + 0.3024295 = 0.8201310. Second column: 9.8776847 + 0.2954097 = 0.1730944. Here log(1+P') is computed from log P' = 0.0027955 (resp. 9.9886858).

(2) Solution by fixed-point iteration. Rough values: x' ≈ 2.0969, x'' ≈ 1.9726 ('Hieraus'). Then:
- x'' = c' − d'(b' − x')/F', with log F' = 0.0065913. From x' = 2.0979020: 8.5509454 − 2.0979020 = 6.4530434; log 0.8097646 + 0.8201310 − 0.0065913 = 1.6233043, i.e. 42.005320; x'' = 43.978893 − 42.005320 = 1.9735738.
- x' = c'' − d''(b'' − x'')/F'', with log F'' = 0.0070416. 5.3744895 − 1.9735738 = 3.4009157; log 0.5315959 + 0.1730944 − 0.0070416 = 0.6976487, i.e. 4.9848109; x' = 7.0827129 − 4.9848109 = 2.0979020.
- So the pair (x', x'') = (2.0979020, 1.9735738) is self-consistent. The earlier trial x'' = 1.9735596 is struck out.

(3) Heliocentric places (right-hand columns). Using log a', log a'' (9.8866898, 9.9972313) and log x' + …, Gauss gets the logs of the radii, 0.3492520 and 0.3443132. The four radii are logs 0.3548982, 0.3492520, 0.3443132, 0.3402653, so r ≈ 2.2 AU. He also gets heliocentric longitudes and checks their differences:
- 49°46'38.63" − 34°49'13.82" = 14°57'24.81".
- 78°9'12.56" − 66°58'2.32" = 11°11'10.24".
- Reductions to the orbit plane use several log-sin/cos lines and angles 18°25'17.75", 17°29'41.71", −8°27'41.89", etc.
- Result: the arcs in the orbit between consecutive observations are 2f = 10°5'50.11", 10°24'59.98", 10°55'16.05". Halves: 5°2'55.055", 5°12'29.99", 5°27'38.025". Quarters: 2°31'27.5275", 2°36'14.995", 2°43'49.0125".

(4) Sector-to-triangle ratios. From the intervals (56462, 49388, 40479 in some time unit; quarters 14115½, 12347, 10119¾), the radii and the half-arcs, Gauss computes the ratio y = sector/triangle for each interval. He uses the series form: the constant 8333333.3 = 10^8/12, and small corrections such as 19473.7 + 106.1. Columns then give log y ≈ 0.0043202, 0.0045400, 0.0049349 (0.0048401 is struck out and corrected).

(5) New hypothesis values: log P' = 0.0026856, log P'' = 9.9888832, log Q' = 9.2375845, log Q'' = 9.2520671. These feed the second iteration on the next page (c' = 43.977141, x' = 2.0953782, …).

In short: one complete cycle of Gauss's iterative 'hypothesis' correction for a four-observation minor-planet orbit.", "errors": ["The first-pass 'Pars constans' paired the small terms with the wrong columns: 37.500571 and 2.5944136.
